system_overview: This specification models an abstract version of the Quicksort sorting algorithm. It is one of the examples from Section 7.3 of 'Proving Safety Properties' by Leslie Lamport. The module defines the algorithm using PlusCal, provides the translated state-machine specification, and includes a structured proof of its partial correctness property: that if the algorithm terminates, it produces a sorted permutation of the original sequence. The specification abstracts away the partition procedure, instead choosing in a single step an arbitrary result that any valid partition procedure could produce.
actors_and_components: The system is a single sequential sorting algorithm. There is one actor: the sort procedure, which repeatedly selects intervals, partitions them, and subdivides the work set until all intervals are singletons. No concurrency is involved.
state_variables: The system maintains: (1) the current sequence being sorted, (2) a copy of the original sequence (used for verifying that the final result is a permutation of the input), (3) a set of intervals still to be processed (each interval is a contiguous range of indices), and (4) a program counter tracking whether the algorithm is still running or has terminated.
initial_state: The sequence is chosen nondeterministically from all non-empty sequences of integers drawn from the specified value set. The original-sequence copy is set equal to the initial sequence. The work set contains a single interval spanning all indices of the sequence. The program counter is set to the main loop label.
actions: The algorithm has one main action corresponding to one iteration of the sorting loop: (1) If the work set is non-empty, select an arbitrary interval from it. If that interval contains exactly one element, simply remove it from the work set. Otherwise, choose a pivot index within the interval, split the interval into a lower subinterval and an upper subinterval around the pivot, nondeterministically choose a new sequence that is a valid partition of the current sequence over the chosen interval and pivot (elements at or below the pivot index are no greater than elements above it, and elements outside the interval are unchanged), update the sequence to this new version, and replace the original interval in the work set with the two new subintervals. (2) If the work set is empty, the algorithm terminates. A stuttering step prevents deadlock after termination.
safety_properties: Partial correctness: when the algorithm terminates, the final sequence is a permutation of the original input sequence and is sorted in non-decreasing order. An inductive invariant is defined involving domain partitions, permutation preservation, and relative sortedness between intervals.
liveness_properties: Termination: the algorithm eventually reaches its terminal state. This is ensured by weak fairness on the transition relation.
model_bounds: The set of allowed integer values is declared as a constant that must be a subset of the integers. For model checking, a companion module redefines the sequence operator to produce only sequences up to a bounded length.
additional_assumptions: The set of values is assumed to be a subset of the integers. Permutations are defined via composition with automorphisms of the domain. The partition operator produces all permutations that leave elements outside the interval unchanged while ensuring elements at or below the pivot are no greater than those above it. The specification includes a partial TLAPS-checked proof of the correctness theorem.
